- A public Go library (`github.com/Espresso-Aficionados/linkclean`) and its `cmd/linkclean` command. A merge to main deploys and publishes nothing: consumers get a change only once a `v*` tag is pushed and they bump to it. Tags are cut by `tools/rulegen release`, either for a rules data update (which also carries any `require`-only dependency bumps merged since the last tag) or by hand, so a merged bump ships with the next release.
- `code.dny.dev/ssrf` is the dial guard of package `unshorten`, the only package that makes network requests (`unshorten/transport.go`, `classify.go`, `errors.go`): it decides which addresses and ports a resolver may connect to, so a change to its default deny lists or its API silently widens or narrows what consumers' servers reach. It is pinned to v0.3.x in `dependabot.yml`; only patch releases come here. `unshorten/ssrf_test.go` and the attestation tests in ci.yml (`TestAttestAfterNew`, `TestTransportCheck`, `TestGuardTransport`) check the guard.
- `golang.org/x/net` provides `idna` (`internal/rawurl/host.go`, `internal/matchpattern/pattern.go`) and `publicsuffix` (`internal/rawurl/site.go`). Both decide how hosts in untrusted URLs are normalised and matched against the rules: a change in IDNA mapping or in the public suffix list changes which rules apply to which URLs, and `golang.org/x/text` (indirect) comes with it. The golden cases (`testdata/golden`, run by `TestRules/Golden` and `linkclean -check` in CI) are the guard there.
- The `tools` module has no dependencies. The GitHub Actions run tests only; the `rules` jobs check out with full history and run `tools/rulegen` against the vendored rule data. No workflow publishes anything.
- `tools/upstream/adblock-lists` (gitsubmodule) is the rules data source: its bumps carry rule changes that `tools/rulegen` syncs into `rules/brave/`, and are never merged as plain dependency updates.
